author: agent
text:
DEFECT found by eye on 2026-08-16, not by any test: the browser tab of EVERY map memway generates reads "memway - itsdangerous, the real map". The title is hardcoded at viz_template.html:6 and export() never overrides it, so it is not a memway.io problem - it ships in the wheel and every user's map claims to be a map of itsdangerous. Verified on maps built by the published 0.54.0 wheel for two unrelated repos: both carry that title, and on the live memway.io/map.html the string "itsdangerous" appears EXACTLY ONCE in 761KB - only in the title - while the body is memway's own 909 entities.

It is a leftover from the registry-demo era, when the flagship map really was itsdangerous. Nothing caught it because the title is a constant, not behaviour: the payload tests, the airgap tests and the executed-predicate tests all pass on a page whose tab lies. This is the same class as the dead lens toggle and the copyable-block placement - three of the last five user-visible defects were invisible to every automated layer and were found by a human looking at the screen.

Second, related defect on the same surface: the header label is f"{repo_p.name}..." (viz.py:227), the DIRECTORY name, so memway's own flagship map is published reading "coordsys-v49" - the pre-rename directory. A project name should come from pyproject/package.json/git remote and fall back to the directory, never lead with it.

Wanted: title derived from the same source as the header, so a map cannot advertise a repo it does not describe, plus a test asserting the emitted title contains the repo label and does NOT contain a hardcoded project name.

author: agent
text:
SUPERSEDES the DEFECT note below it. Fixed in 0.54.1; that note is history now. The browser tab no longer claims to be a map of itsdangerous.

What is true now: viz.map_label is THE derivation for a rendered map's label, and the header and the browser title are two uses of ONE call. export() sets payload["repo"] from it; render() substitutes the same value into the __MEMWAY_TITLE__ slot in the template. The point is not the string - it is that the two can no longer drift apart. Verified on the published 0.54.1 wheel: a stranger's map of an unrelated repo emits <title>memway - amb - 9 entities / 6 edges</title>, and "itsdangerous" appears zero times in the page.

STILL WRONG, DELIBERATELY, AND SCHEDULED: map_label builds the name from repo_p.name, the DIRECTORY, so this project's own flagship map publishes as "coordsys-v49" - the pre-rename directory. That is a strict improvement on naming somebody else's project, and it is not the end state. 0.54.2 replaces it at this single source with a precedence chain (pyproject [project].name -> package.json name -> git remote basename -> directory last), after which it reads "memway". Anyone reading between the releases should file the stale directory name as known, not new.

Because title and header now share one source, that change must require ZERO template edits. If it needs one, the 0.54.1 unification was done wrong and the right move is to fix the unification, not to patch the template.

No guard clause on the slot substitution, on purpose: if the slot goes missing the literal survives into the title and tests/test_viz.py fails loudly - the same protection with less machinery.

author: cli
text: Re-read at 0.56.2. Both fence comments still hold - load_existing(write_cache=False) and EdgeBuilder.load(..., write_cache=False), and the fence is still only as strong as its leakiest loader. FIXED here: the render summary counted every entry carrying k['stale'], so it printed '81 stale' on a repo whose decisive queue was 0 - the 81 were superseded history somebody had already answered. It asks unsuperseded_stale now. The rings were never wrong; only the number a human reads was. Fourth appearance of this shape after attention (0.55.2), the queue truncation (0.55.4) and module rot (0.56.1), which is why tests/test_published_map.py pins it.
